task: Write one sentence of your own using the word denounce. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know denounce should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: It took the astronomy board less than a day to denounce the auction of forged meteorites being run under its name.
To mutter against a decision is the faintest protest, complaint kept under the breath where it risks nothing; to denounce it is to condemn it at full volume, in front of everyone.
To object is to state, in so many words, that you disagree; denounce goes further — it condemns in full voice, before an audience, and it means to leave a mark.

To accuse is to name a wrongdoer and a charge — and it can happen in a courtroom, a kitchen, or a private letter. Denounce needs more: a public stage, and a moral judgment pronounced from it, the wrong held up for an audience to condemn.

To attack is to assail in any register — fair or foul, whispered or broadcast — and the word says nothing about the setting or the speaker's standing. Denounce is narrower: condemnation delivered publicly and officially, meant to leave a mark before an audience.
